description: Browser-based Space Invaders arcade game using vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with canvas rendering, progressive difficulty, and clean modern UI

userStories.title: Project setup and game page shell
userStories.description: As a user, I want to open the game in my browser so that I can see the game page and start playing.
acceptanceCriteria: Create index.html, style.css, and game.js as separate files — no inline styles or scripts
index.html links to style.css via <link> and game.js via <script>
Page displays a centered title 'Space Invaders' and an 800x600 canvas element
A 'Start Game' button is visible below or overlaying the canvas
Page has a clean modern look: dark background, sans-serif font, good contrast, centered layout with max-width ~800px
Start a Python HTTP server (python -m http.server) and verify the page loads correctly
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: separate files, centered layout, dark modern UI, Start Game button visible

userStories.title: Game loop and player ship rendering
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see my ship on the canvas when the game starts so that I know the game is running.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking 'Start Game' or pressing Enter hides the start overlay and begins the game loop
Game loop uses requestAnimationFrame with delta-time for frame-rate independent updates
A player ship is drawn near the bottom-center of the canvas using simple geometric shapes
Score displays at top-left starting at 0, lives display at top-right starting at 3
HUD text uses a clean readable font and does not overlap gameplay area
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: Start Game hides overlay, game loop runs, ship drawn at bottom-center, HUD shows Score/Wave/Lives

userStories.title: Player movement controls
userStories.description: As a user, I want to move my ship left and right using the keyboard so that I can dodge enemy fire and aim.
acceptanceCriteria: Left arrow key or A moves the ship left
Right arrow key or D moves the ship right
Ship cannot move beyond the left or right edge of the canvas
Movement is smooth and frame-rate independent (uses delta-time)
Input uses keydown/keyup listeners for responsive held-key movement
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: arrow keys and WASD move ship, clamped to canvas edges, delta-time movement

userStories.title: Player shooting
userStories.description: As a user, I want to fire projectiles upward so that I can destroy aliens.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing Space fires a projectile from the ship's current position
Projectile travels upward at a consistent speed
Only one player projectile can be on screen at a time
Projectile disappears when it leaves the top of the canvas
Projectile is visually distinct (e.g., bright color, small rectangle)
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: Space fires green projectile, one at a time, disappears off-screen

userStories.title: Alien grid formation and movement
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see a grid of alien invaders that move across and down the screen so that there is a threat to respond to.
acceptanceCriteria: Aliens are arranged in a 5-row x 11-column grid
At least 2-3 visually distinct alien types across different rows
The grid moves horizontally together at a consistent speed
When any alien reaches a screen edge, the entire grid drops down one row and reverses horizontal direction
Aliens are rendered clearly using simple geometric shapes against the dark background
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: 5x11 grid, 3 distinct types (diamonds, rounded rects, rects), horizontal movement with drop and reverse

userStories.title: Player-to-alien collision and scoring
userStories.description: As a user, I want my shots to destroy aliens and earn points so that I can progress through the game.
acceptanceCriteria: When a player projectile overlaps an alien (AABB collision), the alien is removed and the projectile disappears
Score increases based on alien row: top row = 30 pts, middle rows = 20 pts, bottom rows = 10 pts
Score display updates immediately on hit
A brief visual effect (flash or color change) plays when an alien is destroyed
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: AABB collision destroys alien, score +10 for bottom row, flash effect, score updates immediately

userStories.title: Alien shooting and alien-to-player collision
userStories.description: As a user, I want aliens to shoot back at me so that the game presents a challenge, and I lose a life when hit.
acceptanceCriteria: Aliens fire projectiles downward at random intervals
Only bottom-row aliens (no alien below them in their column) can fire
Alien projectiles are visually distinct from the player projectile
When an alien projectile hits the player ship (AABB collision), the player loses one life
Lives display updates immediately
A brief visual effect plays on the player ship when hit
Player has ~2 seconds of invulnerability after being hit
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: aliens fire red bullets downward, bottom-row only, player loses life on hit, invulnerability blink works

userStories.title: Progressive difficulty and wave system
userStories.description: As a user, I want the game to get harder as I play so that it stays challenging.
acceptanceCriteria: Alien movement speed increases as aliens are destroyed (fewer aliens = faster)
Alien fire rate increases as aliens are destroyed
When all aliens are destroyed, a new wave spawns with a higher base speed
Wave number is tracked and displayed in the HUD
Each new wave is noticeably harder than the previous one
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: speed scales with alien count and wave number, wave counter in HUD, new wave spawns on clear

userStories.title: Game over screen and restart
userStories.description: As a user, I want a clear game-over screen when I lose so that I know the game ended and can see my score.
acceptanceCriteria: Game ends when lives reach 0 OR when any alien reaches the player's vertical row
Game loop stops completely — no lingering animations or processing
A game-over overlay displays 'Game Over' and the final score
A 'Play Again' button resets all state and starts a new game
The final score is exposed via a JavaScript custom event or callback function for future leaderboard integration
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verified: game over overlay shows score, loop stops (running=false), Play Again resets all state, custom 'gameOver' event dispatched
